note: Agents with a new mechanism, target or modality that are not yet approved for marginal zone lymphoma in the US or EU, selected from peer-reviewed early-phase trials and major meetings. Early response rates often fall with more patients and longer follow-up; meeting data are not peer-reviewed.
scope: One list for all four subtypes, because early-phase trials enroll marginal zone lymphoma as a single cohort. The evidence is thin for several entries, and that is stated in each.

items.tgt: CD20 on B cells and CD3 on T cells
items.why: A T-cell engaging antibody given off the shelf, tested in a cohort of its own for marginal zone lymphoma (extranodal, nodal and splenic) after at least two lines of therapy.
items.data: ELM-2, marginal zone cohort (ASH 2024, abstract 862): ORR 77.1% (95% CI 59.9-89.6), all responses complete; 12-month duration of response 80.2%; median follow-up about 11 months; response rates reported as consistent across subtypes.
items.safety: Cytokine release syndrome in 54.8%, all grade 1-2; grade 3 or higher adverse events in 83.3%, most often neutropenia (23.8%); no immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity reported.
items.next: OLYMPIA-5 (NCT06149286): odronextamab with lenalidomide vs rituximab with lenalidomide in relapsed follicular and marginal zone lymphoma.

items.tgt: CD20 on B cells and CD3 on T cells
items.ev: Peer-reviewed phase 2 (mostly follicular lymphoma); phase 2 meeting data in marginal zone lymphoma
items.why: A fixed-duration, outpatient T-cell engaging antibody approved for follicular lymphoma and now tested as first treatment of marginal zone lymphoma, without chemotherapy.
items.data: MorningSun, untreated marginal zone cohort (SOHO 2025): 36 patients, ORR 77.8% and complete response 64%; 12-month duration of response 92.3%; median follow-up 18.2 months. A response-adapted trial in untreated indolent lymphoma (42 patients, 88% follicular): complete response 71% with mosunetuzumab alone and 86% at the end of treatment; 2-year PFS 89%.
items.safety: MorningSun: cytokine release syndrome in 36.1%, all grade 1-2. Response-adapted trial: cytokine release syndrome in 64%, all grade 1.
items.next: MARSUN (NCT06006117): mosunetuzumab-lenalidomide vs investigator's choice in relapsed marginal zone lymphoma; S2506 (NCT07638722): mosunetuzumab alone or with zanubrutinib or polatuzumab vedotin.

items.ev: Phase 1, meeting data (not yet peer-reviewed); figures not verified here
items.why: Degrading BTK, rather than blocking it, can work against the BTK mutations that cause resistance to covalent and noncovalent BTK inhibitors, the main need after a BTK inhibitor.
items.data: CaDAnCe-101 has a marginal zone lymphoma cohort, with updated results presented at ASH 2025 together with follicular lymphoma; the response rate for marginal zone lymphoma could not be verified from a primary source for this page.
items.next: No phase 3 trial in marginal zone lymphoma was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov when checked.

items.ev: Phase 1, meeting data (not yet peer-reviewed); figures not verified here
items.why: A next-generation BCL2 inhibitor. No BCL2 inhibitor is approved for marginal zone lymphoma, and venetoclax has been little studied in it.
items.data: The phase 1 trial (BGB-11417-101) reported responses to sonrotoclax alone in relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma; response rates could not be verified from a primary source for this page.
items.next: No phase 3 trial in marginal zone lymphoma was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov when checked.
